SELECTED_INDEX: 10
CONFIDENCE: 0.9
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows the classic Raman fingerprint of cyclohexanone.  
• A single strong C=O stretch at 1710 cm⁻¹ matches a saturated cyclic ketone.  
• No 1375 cm⁻¹ CH₃ bend is seen, indicating the molecule is CH₂-rich and methyl-free – consistent with cyclohexanone but not candidates 1, 2, 6 or 7 which all contain CH₃ groups.  
• Ringed CH₂ modes of cyclohexanone are reproduced: 1446 cm⁻¹ (CH₂ scissor), 1298/1269 cm⁻¹ (CH₂ twist/wag), 1137 and 1032 cm⁻¹ (C–C/CH₂ rocking), 834 and 775 cm⁻¹ (ring breathing/deformation) and 611 cm⁻¹ (ring puckering).  
• Aliphatic C–H stretches appear at 2934 and 2861 cm⁻¹, exactly where CH₂ stretches of a cyclohexane ring occur.  
Among the candidates, only 10 (O=C1CCCCC1) is an unmethylated cyclohexanone whose expected Raman bands align with every observed peak.
